item.title: Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said . Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11. Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together. How the scheme worked From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors said. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information. The group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over. The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims. The BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme. From Scotland to a California courtroom Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC said . Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim. Buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples. Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed , that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since. What Scattered Spider is Reuters has described Scattered Spider as a loose-knit community of hackers suspected of breaking into dozens of U.S. companies. item.title: Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds Binance says it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers. Reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to. “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss said. What is frozen Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report . That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it says was affected. Most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts. The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice says government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva said the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action. How the hack unfolded Binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the company said. From there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance. The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has said the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster. That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. The stolen BTC is not covered by those freezes and can be stopped only if it reaches an exchange or service that blocks it. item.title: Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’ K33 Research said bitcoin is trading in “deep value territory” after a 14% weekly drop, arguing that “any entry below $70K is a gift from the market” for medium- to long-term investors. The call comes in the firm’s weekly report, “No gain, plenty of pain,” which published Nov. 16. Head of research Vetle Lunde wrote that bitcoin’s slide has erased its August and September gains and left the market deeply oversold. Bitcoin has posted six straight red weekly candles and is on track for a record 13 consecutive days of lower daily highs, according to K33. Lunde said a streak of six weekly losses has happened only twice before, from Jan. 26 to March 1, 2026, and from April 3 to May 29, 2022. Daily RSI, a momentum gauge, hit 19.95 on Saturday and has stayed below 25 since Friday. Bitcoin also fell below its 200-week moving average, near $68,000, after its worst weekly return since June 7. Bitcoin below its long-term average At the bottom on Nov. 15, bitcoin traded about 8.5% under the 200-week average, a wider gap than the 7.3% recorded at June’s low of $58,500. K33 said 51.5% of the bitcoin supply last moved on-chain at prices above the current level, meaning the average holder could have sold for more at some point in the past four years. Lunde said those readings, taken together, have typically lined up with market bottoms. K33 also noted that crypto has lagged traditional markets, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recovering modestly last week while bitcoin sank. Bitcoin was trading near $62,300 on Wednesday, according to Coinbase spot prices, below the roughly $65,000 level cited in the K33 report, which showed bitcoin down 14% on the week and about 20% over 30 days. Ether also fell 14% over the week, to around $1,827. Outflows, liquidations and hedging Capital continues to leave bitcoin funds. Net outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded products reached 44,900 BTC over the 14 trading days since Oct. 29, K33 said, short of the record of about 71,000 BTC set in June. Total ETF holdings fell to about 1.46 million BTC, the lowest since Aug. 19, and leveraged ETF exposure dropped to 21,900 BTC, the lowest since March 2024. Forced selling hit derivatives, too. About $1.3 billion in long positions were liquidated on Nov. 13 and 14 as bitcoin broke below $70,000, K33 said, and funding rates on perpetual futures repeatedly turned negative. Open interest fell by about 30,000 BTC but stayed above 330,000 BTC, leaving leverage elevated against historical norms. Institutional futures players largely stayed on the sidelines. Open interest in bitcoin futures on CME stayed below 100,000 BTC all week, K33 said, a sign that regulated-market participants have not rushed in to buy the dip. Demand for downside protection is also surging. item.title: Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout Ionic Digital (IOND) sold about 737 bitcoin after the end of September for roughly $61.6 million and plans to spend the money building out its data center sites, the miner built from Celsius’ old mining business disclosed in its latest quarterly report. The company said in its 10-Q that the coins sold at an average of $83,600 each, net of trading costs. The sales cut its bitcoin holdings by about 25% from the Sept. 30 balance. Ionic held 2,954 bitcoin at the end of the third quarter, up from 2,719 at the end of 2025. That implies about 2,217 bitcoin left after the sales. “The Company intends to use the proceeds to fund the development of its existing data center sites,” the filing said. The filing does not say when the coins were sold. Bitcoin traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, about 23% below Ionic’s average sale price. From Celsius miner to landlord Ionic was formed in January 2024 to take over the assets of Celsius Mining under the bankrupt lender’s Chapter 11 plan. It started out as a pure bitcoin miner, running fleets of ASIC machines at its own and hosted sites. That changed in October 2025, when it signed a lease with a single tenant for its Ward County, Texas, facility, which it previously called Cedarvale. The lease runs through January 2037. The third quarter shows how far the shift has gone, with revenue rising to about $49.0 million from $37.1 million a year earlier. Digital infrastructure leasing brought in $43.9 million of that, while mining revenue fell to $5.1 million from $37.1 million. Ionic swung to a net profit of $17.4 million for the quarter, compared with a $4.5 million loss a year earlier. That result included a $73.2 million gain on the fair value of its bitcoin, offset in part by a $65.9 million loss from remeasuring warrants. For the first nine months of the year, Ionic posted a net loss of $30.9 million. More capacity for the tenant In February, Ionic amended the Ward County lease. The tenant is now obligated to lease another 89 megawatts of capacity when it becomes available. Control of that added capacity had not passed to the tenant by the end of September, so Ionic has not booked any revenue on it. The company also had about $19.6 million left to pay on transformer purchases and a substation expansion at the site. The conversion has cost Ionic mining capacity. The company said it does not have room at its owned and leased sites to relocate all of the miners it used to run, so it has decommissioned some of them. Ionic went public through a direct listing on July 28 and raised $400 million in a private placement before $16.7 million in costs. It had about $381.4 million in cash and equivalents at Sept. 30. item.title: German Court Offers to Drop Movie2k Case for 40,000 Bitcoin
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine German Court Offers to Drop Movie2k Case for 40,000 Bitcoin A Leipzig judge last week offered to dismiss the criminal case against the alleged operator of the defunct Movie2k piracy site if he hands over 40,000 bitcoin, a stake worth about $2.56 billion at current prices. The presiding judge at the Leipzig Regional Court, Karsten Nickel, made the proposal in a trial that began in February. A spokesman for the Dresden prosecutors’ office confirmed it after German newspapers and the public broadcaster MDR first reported the offer. Heise later published a detailed account. The trial is before the court’s economic criminal chamber, and the Leipzig court itself had not issued its own confirmation when prosecutors spoke to reporters. Prosecutors believe the defendant still holds about 56,000 bitcoin, and transferring 40,000 would leave him roughly 16,000 coins. At a bitcoin price of about $64,000, those 16,000 coins would be worth about $1.02 billion, and forty thousand bitcoin would be worth about $2.56 billion at the same price. The dollar figures are approximate. Cash, a waiver and leftover coins The proposal also calls for him to pay €38 million in compensation for potential victims, including film rights holders, MDR reported . He would also have to give up any claim to the roughly €2.64 billion Saxony already raised from bitcoin he transferred in 2024, the newspaper Freie Presse reported . Even after handing over most of the remaining coins, he could leave court a billionaire. Movie2k.to ran from 2008 until it was shut down in May 2013. Prosecutors say its operators made millions from advertising contracts and used the proceeds to buy bitcoin when the price was far lower. The defendant is charged with commercial money laundering in 146 cases. The court has already ruled that about 220,000 copyright counts are time-barred and are no longer part of the Movie2k case. A co-defendant, a Polish national, is charged with money laundering in 46 cases and especially serious tax evasion. Prosecutors say he received bitcoin from the main defendant in May 2013 as pay for work on the site. Nickel has said that proof of some of the charges would face “great difficulties.” It is conceivable, he said, that legally and illegally obtained bitcoin were mixed in the accounts. German authorities already sold nearly 50,000 bitcoin German authorities had sought the defendant internationally since late 2019. He was arrested abroad in May 2023 and held in pretrial detention in Saxony until mid-January 2024. On Jan. 16, 2024, he voluntarily transferred about 49,858 bitcoin to wallets provided by the Federal Criminal Police Office. At the time, the coins were worth about €1.96 billion, and he was released from detention around the time of that transfer. Saxony sold the coins between June 19 and July 12, 2024, with support from the Federal Criminal Police Office, for €2,639,683,413.92, or about €2.64 billion. item.title: Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam Coinbase (COIN) said its AI scam-prevention agent stopped about $4.7 million in customer funds from reaching scammers who used a deepfake of Elon Musk to pitch a fake Tesla crypto giveaway, blocking roughly 91% of the money customers tried to send. The exchange described the incident in a Tuesday blog post, part of a weekly series on consumer protection. It said the system worked “with no humans in the loop.” Those two figures imply customers tried to send about $5.2 million, and that roughly $460,000 still left their accounts. Coinbase did not say how much reached the scammers. A livestream that wasn’t real The scam ran during Tesla’s “flying car” demo. Scammers set up a YouTube livestream that looked like the real broadcast, with a deepfake Musk, on-screen wallet addresses and a QR code. The stream promised to double any crypto sent to it, and more than half a million people watched, Coinbase said. Over about two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers tried to send millions of dollars to the addresses on screen. Many were long-time users. Coinbase did not say when the fake stream ran or which coins customers tried to send. The company stressed that its platform was not breached. “Nobody was hacked,” Coinbase wrote. “No Coinbase account was broken into, no password stolen, no credential phished.” That is what makes giveaway fraud hard to stop, since most defenses look for activity the account holder did not authorize, and here the customers logged in and pressed confirm themselves. “Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent,” the post said. How the agent works Coinbase said its defense has three parts. Machine learning models first score outgoing sends in real time, watching for giveaway patterns, brand impersonation and newly created wallet addresses. The goal, the company wrote, is “to catch the danger, not the customer.” When a send is flagged, a scam-specific agent takes over, looking up context, naming the scam pattern, explaining how giveaway schemes work and asking questions meant to make the story fall apart. Each reply is scored for confidence before the customer sees it, so the system knows when a situation needs more friction. The agent had never been trained on this kind of con, Coinbase said. Deepfake giveaways tied to a live product launch were not in its training data. “It recognized the shape of the scheme anyway,” the company wrote, pointing to the promise to multiply funds, the deadline of a live event and a transfer that could not be reversed. Cheaper fakes Coinbase said deepfakes have changed the economics of the scam. Staging something like this once took “a crew, a studio, and weeks,” it wrote. “Now it takes a livestream slot and a model.” The company said it is expanding AI review of risky sends to every type of scam, not just high-profile ones, and is also using AI to label new scam cases so its models learn fro

item.title: New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10% The New York State Common Retirement Fund raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than 10% in the third quarter, to 352,850 shares worth $54.0 million at Sept. 30. The pension fund disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Tuesday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It added 33,000 shares from the 319,850 it reported at June 30. That is an increase of a little more than 10%. The filing does not say why the pension fund added the shares. The reported value nearly doubled, to $54.0 million from $27.8 million. Strategy’s stock closed the quarter at $153.09, up from $86.93 at midyear, so most of the gain in dollar value came from the rally, not from the added shares. A small slice of a large pension fund The fund is one of the largest public pension plans in the U.S. It holds the assets used to pay retirement benefits for New York’s state and local public employees. Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli, the fund’s trustee, valued it at an estimated $309.7 billion as of June 30, the latest official figure. There is not yet a published valuation for Sept. 30. Public equities are only part of the portfolio. As of March 31, they accounted for 39.4% of the fund’s assets, with the rest in cash and bonds, private equity, real estate and other alternatives. The 13F lists 2,975 holdings worth $71.3 billion. The Strategy stake is a small slice of that book, less than a tenth of a percent. Strategy has made bitcoin its primary treasury asset. The company held 850,849 bitcoin as of Nov. 15, with an aggregate purchase price of $64.20 billion, or $75,452 a coin. Institutional managers have 45 days after quarter-end to file a 13F. Tuesday’s report is the first official look at the pension fund’s third-quarter buying, after the stock had already fallen sharply from the $153.09 price used in the filing. Strategy shares have already fallen Strategy closed Tuesday at $96.50, below $100 and about 37% under its Sept. 30 close. At that price, the same 352,850 shares are worth about $34 million, roughly $20 million less than the value in the filing. The common shares also finished under Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, which closed at $98.70. That is the first time they have closed below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close of $121.07. A 13F is a snapshot. It does not show whether the pension fund bought or sold shares in October or November, when most of that decline took place. Coinbase and miners, but no bitcoin ETFs The information table lists no shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust or other spot bitcoin ETFs, and no shares of Strategy’s preferred stock. The pension fund does hold Coinbase (COIN). It reported 109,433 shares at Sept. 30, a little below the 111,633 shares it held at midyear. The reported value still rose, to $20.4 million from $16.3 million, as Coinbase’s stock climbed. It also holds a string of bitcoin miners.

item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine data, as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point rate hike is probably needed in December. The bitcoin price had slipped below $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon. It climbed back to about $65,000 that evening after Nvidia beat earnings estimates, then faded through the U.S. morning. The bitcoin price is down about 21% from a month ago, when it traded above $81,000. Waller floats a half-point hike Waller told CNBC in a live interview that the Fed probably needs a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He said the central bank should reverse its three quarter-point cuts from last year and may need to do more. “You might need to, like, shock people,” Waller said. “I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” he said. Waller said the Fed should deliver the larger move if it is not prepared to signal a faster pace of hikes in the coming months. He also said about 70% of items in the core services basket are running above 3%, which has nothing to do with oil. The 2-year Treasury yield rose more than 4 basis points to 4.83% after his comments. The dollar hit a 19-month high, and gold dropped 2.5% to its lowest level in more than a year. Futures markets fully price a quarter-point hike in December and another increase in January, CNBC reported. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested Tuesday that as many as four hikes could come by spring. Minutes from the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting are due Wednesday afternoon. Policymakers held rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, with Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Nvidia lifts tech stocks Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion after the bell Tuesday, more than double a year earlier and above the $109.1 billion analysts expected. Data center revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, and the company guided to about $130 billion for the current quarter. Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will remain “disciplined in how we commit capital.” The board said it would not reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO last week. item.title: South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says South Korea’s Financial Services Commission plans to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report . The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release. The FSC itself has not publicly announced a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025. A roadmap that stalled That plan opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit. Exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived. The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate. What the Basic Act adds The Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week. Lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Min Byung-duk of the Democratic Party said at a recent forum that he intends to “wrap it up by Jan. 9.” The 5% question The report did not describe what the corporate guidelines will contain. In January, *Seoul Economic Daily* reported that a draft would cap a company’s annual crypto investment at 5% of equity capital and limit purchases to the top 20 coins by market value.
